title: Applied ML Evals: Integrated Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Maya Patel
summary: Canonical playbook that consolidates guidance for the eval harness, maintenance of prompt sets & benchmarks, model onboarding checklists, quality guardrails, quantization profiling, and regression triage procedures used by Applied ML teams at Redwood Inference.
content:
Introduction

Purpose: this doc is the single-source playbook for Applied ML teams to run continuous evaluations, maintain prompt sets and benchmarks, onboard new model variants into the serving catalog, apply quantization profiles safely, and run regression triage when quality or safety metrics drift. Intended audience: applied ML engineers, model owners, SREs supporting inference, and product stakeholders.

Scope: eval harness (CI + daily runs), prompt set lifecycle, model onboarding requirements, quality & safety guardrails, quantization profiling guidelines, and an incident-style regression triage playbook.

1) Eval Harness (CI + Scheduled Runs)

Intro: The eval harness is the automated framework that runs unit, integration, and production-sampling tests against candidate models and production variants. It consists of:
- Local dev harness (pytest-based harness with reference fixtures)
- CI integration (GitHub Actions workflow: eval-harness-ci)
- Nightly jobs (k8s CronJob eval-harness-nightly in namespace applied-ml-evals)
- Canary rollout checks (lightweight runs against canary traffic)

Key metrics produced:
- Accuracy / utility metrics per prompt set (task-specific: F1, BLEU, EM where applicable)
- Safety regressions: toxic-word rate, hallucination rate (as measured by model-specific detectors), PII leakage checks
- Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) on representative inputs
- Token-level correctness & BLEU-like metrics for structured outputs

SLOs for the Eval System:
- CI eval completion: 90% of model PRs finish full eval within 60 minutes
- Nightly coverage: 100% of production-serving models run nightly on core prompt sets
- Regression alert latency: triage ticket created within 1 hour of alert

Usage patterns and ownership:
- Owners: applied-ml-evals team (primary), model-owner (secondary)
- How to run locally: `make eval-run MODEL=<model-id> SUITE=<suite-name>`
- CI labels: add `eval-required` to PRs that change model code, tokenizer, or prompt templates

2) Prompt Sets and Benchmarks

Guiding principles:
- Representativeness: prompt sets should reflect production request distributions and targeted edge cases (internationalization, short/long inputs, structured/JSON inputs)
- Determinism: each prompt set must have seeds and canonical post-processing to ensure reproducible metrics
- Versioning: prompt sets are immutable once published; new versions must use semver-like suffix (e.g., credit-card-classify-v1 -> v2)

Prompt catalog requirements (per prompt set):
- Owner: GitHub handle / OWNING_TEAM
- Description: short summary and intended use-case
- Size: recommended 500-5,000 examples depending on task; smaller targeted sets (50-200) for regression-focused checks
- Tags: task, languages, safety, structured-output, latency-sensitive
- Golden labels: where applicable, provide a gold label file in canonical JSONL format

Benchmarking cadence:
- Nightly: core prompt sets (production-critical)
- Weekly: extended benchmarks (cost/throughput focused)
- On-request: customer-specific benchmarks (run under NDAs)

CI checks for prompt changes:
1. Add new prompt set PR with metadata and sample validation (50 samples)
2. Automated smoke run that verifies format + seed stability
3. Reviewer: applied-ml-evals team + model owner

3) Model Onboarding Guide (serving catalog)

Purpose: Minimum checklist to move a model from research -> serving catalog (hosted/dedicated/private).

Onboarding checklist (must-pass items):
- Model card: architecture, training data summary, license, and known limitations
- Compatibility test: tokenization equivalence check vs canonical tokenizer (failure if >0.1% mismatches on sample corpus)
- Eval harness: run full eval suite (nightly core sets) and compare against baseline model (baseline_id) using the acceptance criteria below
- Latency/throughput targets: specify expected p95 latency and qps at target batch sizes on benchmark hardware (e.g., p95 <= 350ms at 8 tokens on A10G for chat-medium workload)
- Quantization profile (if applicable): recommended config + accuracy delta summary
- Security & privacy review completed for Private deployments (KMS integration, data residency)
- Rollout plan: canary size, rollback triggers, and monitoring dashboards defined

Model acceptance criteria (example):
- Utility: no more than 3% relative drop in task-specific accuracy vs baseline for core prompt sets
- Safety: no increase >0.5 percentage points in toxic-word rate or PII leakage as measured by the safety detectors
- Latency: measurable p95 increase no more than 20% vs baseline for same hardware and batch config

Deployment rollout policy:
1. Canary 1% traffic for 24 hours; automated smoke eval every hour
2. Canary 10% for 12 hours; manual review of logged failures
3. Ramp to 50% with continuous monitoring for 48 hours
4. Full rollout if no major alerts; rollback if any safety/utility thresholds tripped

4) Quality Guardrails (automated and manual controls)

Objectives: Prevent regressions in safety and utility while balancing latency and cost.

Automated guardrails:
- Pre-commit checks: tokenization and schema validation for structured outputs
- CI gating: if safety metric delta > 0.5pp or utility delta > 3% (relative), block merge with mandatory reviewer override
- Runtime checks: per-response safety detectors that increment alert counters; if error rate > threshold, trigger fallback

Runtime thresholds (examples):
- Toxic-word rate alerting threshold: 0.75% (P1 if >1.5%)
- Hallucination proxy (fact-checker score < 0.6): alert at 5% of responses in sampled window (P2)
- PII detector match: any positive detection from structured PII detector triggers immediate disable for that route until investigated

Fallback strategies:
- Model fallback: route to previously validated model variant (fallback_model_id)
- Response rewrite: redact detected PII and re-run a short-context clarification prompt
- Rate-limited degraded mode: serve cached responses for high-volume identical prompts to reduce exposure

5) Quantization Profiles and Safety Checklist

Purpose: document recommended quantization profiles, expected throughput/cost upsides, and acceptable accuracy deltas per model family.

Profile table (ASCII):
Model Family | Profile Name       | Format | Expected throughput uplift | Typical accuracy delta (task avg)
------------ | ------------------ | ------ | -------------------------: | -------------------------
Llama-2-13B  | int8-e4m2          | int8   | 1.6x                      | -0.8%
Llama-2-70B  | q4f16              | q4_16  | 2.3x                      | -1.5%
Redwood-Chat | int8-e4m2-guard    | int8   | 1.5x                      | -0.5%
StableLM-7B  | q4_0               | q4_0   | 1.8x                      | -0.7%

Quantization safe-steps:
1. Run per-layer sensitivity analysis with the eval harness using core prompt sets (script: tools/quant/profile_layer_sensitivity.py)
2. Generate accuracy vs throughput curve and annotate acceptable pareto point with model owner
3. Produce a quantization profile artifact (YAML) that includes fallback_bitwidths, blocked-layers, and checksum
4. CI gating: any profile that increases safety metric >0.25pp must be rejected
5. Canary quantized model only on dedicated non-production capacity for 48 hours before serving to customers

6) Regression Triage Playbook

Triggers:
- CI alert (post-PR): failing eval scenario beyond configured thresholds
- Monitoring alert: nightly or runtime alert for quality/safety drift
- Customer report: escalated support case with reproducible prompt(s)

Initial triage steps (within 1 hour):
1. Create a triage ticket in Tracker (tag: regression-triage) and assign oncall applied-ml-evals
2. Gather artifacts: model version, prompt set name + example prompts, eval results, runtime request logs (sampled), and recent deployments
3. Run regression reproduction job (script: tools/regression/reproduce.sh) against both current and baseline models
4. Classify regression:
   a) Data drift / prompt distribution change
   b) Model-caused (training or tokenization change)
   c) Quantization-induced
   d) Serving infra (latency/timeouts)

Resolution path examples:
- If quantization-induced: disable quantized variant, revert to full-precision variant, and open quantization profile update task
- If model-caused: rollback deployment or apply quick patch (e.g., prompt-template fix) and schedule deeper analysis with model-owner
- If data drift: move prompt into monitoring set, consider retraining or prompt-engineering; alert product owner for UX changes

Postmortem requirements for P1/P2 regressions:
- Timeline of events, root cause classification, impact metrics (% requests affected, customer impacts), corrective actions, and planned mitigations
- Owner and ETA for each action item
- Publish to confluence under applied-ml-and-evals/postmortems within 72 hours

7) Operational Playbook and Dashboards

Required dashboards:
- Eval health dashboard: job success rates, CI durations, nightly job coverage
- Quality trend dashboard: per-model safety/utility metrics over rolling 30 days
- Canary dashboard: per-canary metrics with automated comparison to baseline

Runbook snippets:
- How to revert a model: `inference-cli revert --model <model-id> --to <baseline-id>` (requires approver from model-owner team)
- How to run quick eval: `python tools/eval/run.py --model <model-id> --suites core,security --out runs/<id>.json`

8) Roles & Responsibilities

- Applied-ML-Evals Team: owns eval harness, prompt catalog governance, nightly jobs, and regression triage coordination
- Model Owner: provides model card, performs pre-onboarding checks, approves quantization pareto points, and owns rollouts
- Serve/SRE: provides hosting capacity for canaries and ensures p95 latency SLOs are met
- Security & Privacy: signs off on Private deployment checklist and PII detectors

Appendices

A. Useful CLI commands and scripts
- `make eval-run MODEL=<id> SUITE=<suite>`
- `tools/quant/profile_layer_sensitivity.py --model <id> --out profile.csv`
- `tools/regression/reproduce.sh --model-current <id> --model-baseline <id> --prompts prompts.jsonl`

B. Contact list
- Applied ML Evals oncall: #applied-ml-evals-oncall (Slack)
- Model-owner rotation: see OWNERS file in model repo
